lists.name: The Yo-Yo Court
lists.idea: Teleport control: Mallex and five Legionaries kill, Fade, and Rapid-Ingress back while the Tzeentch castle holds under the boons.
lists.doctrine: Learn on this one — every model owned and painted.

lists.name: The Festering Court
lists.idea: Nurgle attrition plus War Dogs: durable objective play, the −1-to-wound boon on the big targets, Karnivores for anti-tank.
lists.doctrine: Waits on Beasts and Plague Drones the audit showed were never in the box.

lists.name: Word Bearers Ascendant
lists.idea: An all-marine deep-strike wave under Be'lakor: two Lords, Terminators, Chosen and Warp Talons arriving where the line is thinnest.
lists.doctrine: The most buying left. Stored with one Cultist Mob instead of two so the Heretic Astartes total (930 + 30 for Fade) stays inside the 1,000 cap even if enhancement points count toward it — the printed version ran two Cultist Mobs at 980 + 30 for exactly 2,000.

lists.name: Crimson Cavalry
lists.idea: Khorne turn-one alpha: a scouting Skullmaster and Bloodcrusher brick, letters and hounds Advancing and still charging under the boon.
lists.doctrine: Opens up if the Khorne lot and the Bloodcrushers crate are generous.

lists.name: The Fadethirster
lists.idea: The tournament silhouette: a Fading Bloodthirster plus the Skullmaster/Bloodcrusher brick and a Rendmaster, cheap daemons scoring underneath.
lists.doctrine: Stored at 1,980: the printed version ran Plague Drones ×3 and came to 2,010 once Skullmaster went to 85, so the (owned) Screamers stand in — swap back or trim elsewhere if you prefer the Drones.

lists.name: Triple Monster
lists.idea: Be'lakor, a Fading Bloodthirster and the Lord of Change: three T10–11 monsters each dragging a 6" shadow bubble own the board by turn two. Beginner-forgiving.
lists.doctrine: Unlocked the moment the Bloodthirster gets his arms — assembly and paint only.

rule_of_three.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k11ed/the-rules/core-rules/ — Muster Armies (assumed standard; not restated in the repo's digests)
rule_of_three.note: Applied flat across battle sizes, as is Dreadblades; only the Thralls cap scales.

army_rule.name: Shadow of Chaos
army_rule.gist: The battlefield divides into in-shadow and not. Your deployment zone is always in your Shadow; No Man's Land is in it at the start of any phase in which you control at least half the objectives there; the enemy zone joins once you control at least half of theirs; Be'lakor and Greater Daemons carry a 6" bubble.

effects.name: Daemonic Manifestation
effects.gist: Friendly daemons in shadow: +1 to Battle-shock tests; a passed test heals D3 wounds, or returns up to D3 destroyed models to a Battleline unit (never Characters, per the July clarification).

effects.name: Daemonic Terror
effects.gist: Enemy units in shadow (or within 6" of a Greater Daemon): −1 to Battle-shock tests and D3 mortal wounds on a failure; Battle-shocked units drop to OC 0 and stop holding objectives.

army_rule.lesson: Fight for the mid-board objectives early: two of three switches the Shadow on across the centre.

detachment.name: Shadow Legion
detachment.gist: Be'lakor's own legion: every god's daemons plus a capped allowance of Chaos Space Marines. Be'lakor and Heretic Astartes gain SHADOW LEGION and UNDIVIDED; Legiones Daemonica gain SHADOW LEGION. 2 of the 3 detachment points available at 2,000; the usual third point goes on Cavalcade of Chaos when Bloodcrushers are in the list.

thralls.name: Thralls of the First Prince
thralls.text: When mustering your army, you cannot include any DAEMON PRINCE, DAEMON PRINCE WITH WINGS or EPIC HERO units (excluding BE'LAKOR), but you can include the following HERETIC ASTARTES units: CHAOS LORD, CHAOS LORD IN TERMINATOR ARMOUR, CHAOS LORD WITH JUMP PACK, CHAOS TERMINATOR SQUAD, CHOSEN, DAMNED units, Dark Apostle, HAVOCS, LEGIONARIES, Master of Possession, Possessed, RAPTORS, SORCERER, SORCERER IN TERMINATOR ARMOUR, WARP TALONS. The combined points value of such units depends on your battle size: Incursion up to 500 pts / Strike Force up to 1000 pts / Onslaught up to 1500 pts.
thralls.damned_note: Cultist Mob qualifies through its DAMNED keyword.
thralls.why: This is what makes the Word Bearers half legal in a daemon army — and what bans a second named centrepiece.
thralls.text_note: Near-verbatim from Wahapedia via docs/research.md (battle-size table flattened into one sentence).

bans.why: Painted lots love a named centrepiece; in this detachment every one but Be'lakor is dead points.

warlord.rule: If Be'lakor is in the army he must be the Warlord (Supreme Commander).

dreadblades.rule: Chaos Knights Dreadblades: an all-Chaos army may include either 1 TITANIC Chaos Knight or up to 3 War Dog models as allies; none may be the Warlord, none may take enhancements, and they get no Shadow Legion boon.
dreadblades.why: It is the only way this army fields anti-tank walkers; verify before a tournament, kitchen tables will not ask.
dreadblades.note: No repo document quotes the rule text; every one that mentions it says verify in the app before an event. Whether the allowance scales with battle size is unaddressed — the linter applies 3 at every size.

enhancements.name: Fade to Darkness
enhancements.gist: If the bearer's unit destroys a unit in the Fight phase and ends outside engagement range, it returns to Strategic Reserves — back next turn (a Chaos Lord re-enters free with Rapid Ingress). The detachment's signature yo-yo; legal on a Bloodthirster.

enhancements.name: Leaping Shadows
enhancements.gist: The bearer's unit gains Scouts 9" — a pre-game move that turns a Skullmaster's Bloodcrushers (or a monster) into a near-certain turn-one charge.

enhancements.name: Malice Made Manifest
enhancements.gist: Start of the Fight phase, pick an enemy unit in Engagement Range and roll a D6: 2–5 = D3 mortal wounds, 6 = 3. Situational; suits a character who will be stuck in every turn.

enhancements.name: Mantle of Gloom
enhancements.gist: Aura: enemy units in Engagement Range of the bearer's unit are −1 OC — helps a mid-board anchor flip a contested objective.

stratagems.name: Channelled Wrath
stratagems.gist: One unit's melee weapons gain Lance (+1 to wound if it charged); a KHORNE unit also gets +1 AP.

stratagems.name: Binding Shadow
stratagems.when: End of the opponent's Fight phase
stratagems.gist: Up to one Heretic Astartes unit and one daemon unit not in Engagement Range go back into Strategic Reserves — the rescue half of the yo-yo.

stratagems.name: Death Denied
stratagems.gist: One unit regains 3 wounds; a TZEENTCH unit also returns one destroyed non-character model.

stratagems.name: Encroaching Darkness
stratagems.gist: Up to one Heretic Astartes and one daemon unit that arrived from Reserves this turn ignore cover.

stratagems.name: Spiteful Demise
stratagems.gist: Roll a D6 per enemy unit in Engagement Range (+2 if SLAANESH): 4–5 = D3 mortal wounds, 6+ = 3.

stratagems.name: Shade Path
stratagems.gist: A visible enemy within 12" that declares a charge gets −1" to it; against a NURGLE unit it also takes a Battle-shock test. (Nerfed from −2" in this edition.)

play_notes: Reserves: at most half your points start off the board; arrivals from battle round 2; anything still in reserve at the end of round 3 is destroyed (core rules, per the Primer).
Deep Strike sets up more than 8" from every enemy model this edition.
One stratagem per unit per phase — spend the command point on the moment, not out of habit.
rules.leaders_note: Leader pairings are stored on each character (leads). A leader entry in a list points at the bodyguard entry it joins; the linter checks the pairing is one the datasheet allows.

other_stratagems.name: Denizens of the Warp
other_stratagems.gist: Deep Strike arrival closer than the usual >8" (the older text says 3"). Listed by the Jul-24 guide and the codex as part of the toolkit, but it is not one of the six Shadow Legion stratagems the Primer verified and it is the obvious errata candidate — check the app before planning around it.

other_stratagems.name: Warp Surge
other_stratagems.gist: A daemon unit inside your Shadow of Chaos charges after Advancing. Listed by the Jul-24 guide/codex; not among the Primer's verified six — may belong to another detachment or the index era. Verify.

secondary_detachments.name: Cavalcade of Chaos
secondary_detachments.gist: Mounted-unit package — Soul-shattering Charge for the big Bloodcrusher unit (it fights at 3" Engagement Range) plus cavalry stratagems; every top-placing Shadow Legion tournament list the Primer studied takes it
secondary_detachments.source: docs/PRIMER.md — Pairing with Cavalcade of Chaos

glossary.means: Munitorum Field Manual — Games Workshop's free points document. v1.1 (2026-07-22) is the snapshot every total here uses; it changes a few times a year, so totals are dated.
Points. A standard game ('Strike Force') is 2,000 points a side; every unit costs a fixed amount per datasheet size (5 Legionaries 90, 10 Legionaries 170).
One unit's rules card. 'Rule of three': at most three of the same datasheet in a 2,000-point army (six if it is Battleline).
The sub-faction rules package an army picks. Shadow Legion is Be'lakor's own; in this edition's system it costs 2 detachment points (DP), which is why the docs say '2 DP'.
The Chaos Daemons detachment for Be'lakor's mixed host: daemons of all four gods plus a capped allowance of Chaos Space Marines, each allegiance getting its own boon.
Chaos Space Marines — the Word Bearers half of this army. 'Thralls of the First Prince' is the rule that lets specific CSM units in, up to 1,000 points at 2,000.
A named, unique character (Skulltaker, Kairos…). Shadow Legion bans every one except Be'lakor, so a named centrepiece in an eBay lot is dead points here.
The model that leads your army for mission purposes. Be'lakor's 'Supreme Commander' rule makes him the Warlord whenever he is present.

Small Chaos Knights (walkers). They are not Shadow Legion units; the Chaos Knights 'Dreadblades' rule lets any Chaos army take up to three War Dog models as allies — never the Warlord, no enhancements.
A paid upgrade for one CHARACTER (not an Epic Hero), each taken once per army. Shadow Legion's four: Fade to Darkness 30, Leaping Shadows 25, Malice Made Manifest 25, Mantle of Gloom 20.
Enhancement: if the bearer's unit kills something in melee and ends out of combat, it goes back into reserve and returns next turn — the 'yo-yo'. Legal on a Bloodthirster.
A character that joins a specific bodyguard unit (Chaos Lord → Legionaries, Bloodmaster → Bloodletters). Lists show it as 'leads'.

Arriving from reserve mid-game, set up more than 8" from every enemy model (this edition); Rapid Ingress is doing so at the end of the opponent's Movement phase (a Chaos Lord does it free once per round).

Core troops (Pink Horrors, Bloodletters, Legionaries, Cultists) — allowed six per army instead of three. For daemon Battleline units it also matters that the army rule can return destroyed models to them.
A leadership test units take when hurt; failing drops Objective Control (OC) to 0, so they stop holding objectives. This army wins by forcing those failures inside Be'lakor's shadow.

Greater Daemons are the big monsters (Bloodthirster, Lord of Change). Heralds are daemon lieutenants — Bloodmaster (on foot), Skullmaster (on a Juggernaut), Rendmaster (on a Blood Throne), Fateskimmer (on a chariot).
Unbuilt plastic still on its frame; New on Sprue; New in Box; assembled but unpainted. Cheaper to buy and faster to paint shadow-first than repainting someone else's work.

How the scorecard grades a lot from its photos: Primer-only (bare or undercoated) · Partial (any unpainted or primed squad in an otherwise painted lot) · Basic · Tabletop · Tabletop+ · High TT · Display. 'Assumed' means nobody has checked the gallery yet.

Landed = price + roughly 3% + estimated shipping (what actually leaves your account). OBO = 'or best offer'. The value ratio is kit retail × paint premium ÷ landed price: ≥1.5× BUY, 0.8–1.49 FAIR, under 0.8 SKIP; auctions are never scored because a bid is not a price.

A read-only, dated pass over eBay for specific units (last run 2026-07-27) — the source of price floors such as "Skullmaster ≈$44". Buy-It-Now only; auctions, flagged and part-kit listings are excluded. Re-run before buying; nothing here is a live offer.

data/muster.json is the one file every number comes from. Edits made in this app stay in the browser; 'export' downloads the updated file and 'patch' copies instructions for a Claude session to apply and commit.
≈ approximate count or cost; ? unknown until the crate is opened; ~ points not verified to the point; 9/10 nine models owned where the smallest legal unit is ten.

In the game a codex is an official army rulebook. On these pages 'the codex' means Codex: The Umbral Creed — the personal army book written for this collection (fiction, unit nicknames, doctrines, the purchase ledger). Quoted names such as “The Source” are its nicknames.
An order that has not been catalogued yet. Its cost counts as spent; its models count for nothing until you open it in crate mode and tick what actually arrived.
Built, painted and based — the state a model must be in to count toward a 'painted' list. 'On sprue', 'assembled', 'primed' and 'damaged' are not table-ready.

When Pink Horrors die they split into Blue Horrors, and Blues into pairs of Brimstone Horrors; the Blue and Brimstone models in the box mostly serve as those free replacements rather than as bought units.

The per-god bonus the Shadow Legion detachment rule hands each unit (Khorne: advance and still shoot/charge; Tzeentch: harder to hit; Nurgle: harder to wound; Slaanesh: immune to snap shooting; Undivided: Dark Pacts).

Toughness, Wounds and Save — the durability numbers on a datasheet (T10–11 is monster-grade). A 'bubble' or aura is a rule that affects everything within the stated distance of the model, e.g. Be'lakor's 6" Shadow of Chaos.

The community-maintained BattleScribe / New Recruit data files. Where a points value here says 'per the BSData transcription' it was read from those files rather than from GW's document — verify in the app.
Games Workshop's Warhammer 40,000 app — the arbiter for current points and rule text. 'Verify / check in the official app' always means that app, not this page.

Three vocabularies meet here: a seller's description ('tabletop paint', 'well painted', 'some damage') is quoted as listed and never trusted; the collection's own paint state per entry (unassembled — shown as 'on sprue' — assembled, primed, basecoated, painted, well painted, damaged) is what you judged in crate mode; the scorecard's tiers (Partial · Basic · Tabletop · Tabletop+ · High TT · Display) grade whole eBay lots from photos.

How a shopping line counts models when a list fields the same datasheet twice — nine Bloodcrushers as a unit of six and a unit of three. 'N more models to complete the owned unit' means topping up models you already have (nine Bloodletters need one more to make a legal ten).

A stratagem is an in-game ability you pay Command Points (CP) to trigger; you gain 1 CP in every Command phase, yours and the opponent's — about two per battle round. Shadow Legion has six; one use per unit per phase this edition.

Table slang. Castle: keep the army tight around its buffs and make the enemy come to you. Screen: cheap units placed to keep chargers and deep-strikers away from valuable ones. Brick: one big unit (six Bloodcrushers). Alpha strike / turn-one alpha: hitting hard before the opponent has moved, e.g. with Scouts + Advance + charge.

Advance: move an extra D6" but normally give up shooting and charging (the Khorne boon removes that penalty). Scouts X": a free move before the first turn. Engagement Range: within 1" of an enemy — 'in combat'.

Snap shooting is this edition's out-of-turn reaction fire, Overwatch included; the Slaanesh boon ignores it. Dark Pacts is the Chaos Space Marine army rule the Undivided boon grants: take a Leadership test before shooting or fighting for Lethal or Sustained Hits, at the risk of mortal wounds.

Dark Vengeance and Blackstone Fortress are older boxed games some models came from (the Cultists; Obsidius Mallex, used as a Chaos Lord). A Juggernaut is Khorne's brass daemon-steed (Bloodcrushers, Skullmaster); the Blood Throne / Skull Cannon kit builds the Rendmaster's chariot. Night Lords, Raptors, Seekers and Tzaangors are units or lots that were considered and not bought; Warp Talons are still wanted for lists C and D. A Cygor and a Deathbringer are unrelated kits two sellers titled 'Bloodthirster'.

Abbreviations in scorecard notes and titles: MSRP (retail price), OOP (out of production), BIN (Buy-It-Now), NIB / NoS (new in box / new on sprue), OBO (or best offer), AoS (Age of Sigmar — same daemon kits), GSC (Genestealer Cults), LoV (a Lord of Virulence, a Death Guard character), MoE (Master of Executions), PM (Plague Marines), MoP (Master of Possession), Jakhals (World Eaters cultists), 'termis' (Terminators). In feed notes 'DP' means a Daemon Prince model, not detachment points.

The Primer is this repo's beginner's guide to playing the army (Library → Learn to play). In paint talk, primer is the undercoat; a 'primed' model or a 'Primer-only' lot has that undercoat and nothing else.
